readingInstruction: Read Daniel 1:1-2:49. A young man taken to Babylon refuses to compromise, and later interprets a king’s dream about a statue and a stone. Notice how Daniel and his friends live as exiles, and notice what the dream says about the kingdoms of the earth.
settingTheScene: Daniel was taken to Babylon as a teenager in 605 BC, in the first deportation. He and three friends were selected to be trained for the king’s service. Daniel is the book that addresses the question of how God’s people live in a foreign empire. It is written partly in Hebrew and partly in Aramaic, the language of international affairs (2:4 to 7:28). It moves from stories of faithfulness in the first six chapters to visions of the future in the last six.
observation: “But Daniel resolved that he would not defile himself with the king’s food” (1:8).
“God gave these four youths learning and skill in all literature and wisdom” (1:17).
“Let the name of God be blessed forever and ever, to whom belong wisdom and might” (2:20).
“He changes times and seasons; he removes kings and sets up kings” (2:21).
“No wise men, enchanters, magicians, or astrologers can show to the king the mystery that the king has asked, but there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries” (2:27-28).
“You, O king, were looking, and behold, a great image” (2:31).
“A stone was cut out by no human hand, and it struck the image on its feet of iron and clay, and broke them in pieces” (2:34).
“And in the days of those kings the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that shall never be destroyed” (2:44).
interpretation:
The first chapter shows the pressure of assimilation. The young men are renamed with Babylonian names that honor Babylonian gods, taught a new language and literature, and given food from the king’s table. Daniel draws a line at the food, probably because it had been offered to idols or violated the law. He does so respectfully, asks for a test, and God honors it. Faithfulness here is both principled and wise. They serve the empire well, and God gives them skill. The lesson is that we can serve in a foreign place without compromising our loyalty to God.

Chapter 2 introduces the first great vision. Nebuchadnezzar has a dream that troubles him, and he demands that his wise men tell him both the dream and its meaning. They cannot. The king orders them all killed, including Daniel. Daniel asks for time and prays with his friends. God reveals the dream in the night. Daniel’s response is a hymn of praise: “Blessed be the name of God forever and ever, to whom belong wisdom and might. He changes times and seasons; he removes kings and sets up kings.” Before he tells the king, he gives God the credit. And in front of the king, he says plainly: “No wise men… can show the king the mystery, but there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries.”

The dream is of a great statue with a head of gold, chest of silver, belly of bronze, legs of iron, and feet of iron mixed with clay. A stone, not cut by human hands, strikes the feet, and the whole statue becomes dust. The stone grows into a mountain that fills the earth. Daniel interprets: the head is Nebuchadnezzar, and the other metals are successive kingdoms. The stone is the kingdom that God will set up, which will never be destroyed. The message is that the great empires of human history will pass, and God’s kingdom will last forever.

Nebuchadnezzar falls on his face and acknowledges Daniel’s God as “God of gods and Lord of kings.” Though the king’s confession is incomplete, it shows that God’s hand can reach even the rulers of the earth.
connection: Jesus is the stone that the builders rejected (Matthew 21:42-44; 1 Peter 2:4-8). Luke 1:33 says of Jesus, “Of his kingdom there will be no end.” Matthew 6:10 teaches us to pray, “Your kingdom come.” Romans 12:2 says, “Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed.” Colossians 2:3 says that in Christ are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge. 1 Peter 2:11-12 calls us to live as exiles with good conduct.
application:
Where do you face pressure to compromise? Decide, as Daniel did, what you will not defile yourself with, and do it graciously.

Pray with friends, as Daniel did, when you face a situation you cannot handle on your own.

Praise God before you ask for his help. Say Daniel 2:20-21 aloud.
prayerPrompts: Bless the name of God, to whom wisdom and might belong.
Ask him to help you stand firm in a foreign place.
Thank him that he changes times and seasons.
